clue.text: Second female is lighter

parts.note: a cow is a female animal, here of cattle

explanation.surface: A remark that the second woman weighs less than someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for ferrying goods, and a scow is just such a boat.

clue.text: They're on the left in 19 across, as opposed to 26

definitions.text: They're on the left in 19 across, as opposed to 26

parts.words: They're on the left in 19 across, as opposed to 26
parts.note: in double-entry bookkeeping these entries go in the left-hand column, and too many of them leave an account in the red rather than in the black

explanation.surface: Something that sits on the left side in red, unlike things in black.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 across is RED and 26 across is BLACK: being 'in the red' means owing money, 'in the black' means in credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Charges against an account are recorded on the left side of a ledger and push a balance into overdraft.

clue.text: Awfully rude in middle of meal? Wonderful!

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit in the centre of the meal word, splitting it into two halves

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of rude are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone shocked by rudeness at dinner, then sarcastically exclaiming how marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' reads as an intensifier for rude, but it signals the scramble, giving ERDU; 'in middle of' means the meal is split in two around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Super-duper is a jaunty, informal exclamation of delight meaning excellent or marvellous.

clue.text: Beef that may be 19 across or 26

definitions.meaning: beef as slang for a complaint or grievance
a game bird found as red and black varieties

explanation.surface: Meat which might be described as red or black.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 across is RED and 26 across is BLACK; the red grouse and black grouse are both British moorland birds.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble is to beef, and the red and black species are well-known game birds.

clue.text: Learned of old coin in river turning up

indicators.note: the coin is placed inside the river word
in a down clue, turning up means the river name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales/England
the ducat was a gold coin of medieval Europe

explanation.surface: Someone schooled about an antique coin found surfacing in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' reads the river upward, giving EED; 'in' then wraps it round the coin. The Dee is a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned and educated are both adjectives describing someone with much schooling and knowledge.

clue.text: Heard complaint that's usually 19 across or 11

indicators.note: heard signals that the word is listened to rather than read

parts.note: a whine is a peevish complaint

explanation.surface: Someone overheard moaning about the usual colour choices.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 across is RED and 11 across is WHITE: wine usually comes in those two colours.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink made from fermented grapes is usually described as either red or white.

clue.text: Hasn't led astray writer about 19 across and 26

indicators.note: led astray means led off course, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that an author has failed to mislead his readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 across is RED and 26 across is BLACK: Stendhal wrote Le Rouge et le Noir (The Red and the Black).
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist's best-known book is titled The Red and the Black.

clue.text: Noble PM, between 11 and 26

definitions.meaning: Earl ..., the 2nd Earl, was a nobleman who served as British Prime Minister
the shade lying between white and black

explanation.surface: A peer serving as Prime Minister, sitting between two others.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 across is WHITE and 26 across is BLACK; Earl Grey was Prime Minister 1830-34 and gave his name to the tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The aristocratic premier bore the surname, and the neutral shade sits midway between the two extremes.

clue.text: Victory sign with 21, 26 and 11

parts.note: the banner waved at the finish of a motor race, patterned in squares of black and white

explanation.surface: A signal of triumph decorated with squares, black and white.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is SQUARES, 26 is BLACK and 11 is WHITE: the motor-racing finishing banner has that checkerboard pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing the winner is the first to see this black-and-white checked banner waved.

clue.text: Put in grave situation in leaderless period of decline

indicators.note: leaderless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: winter, figuratively, is a season of decline, as in the winter of life

explanation.surface: Someone placed in a dire predicament during a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in grave situation' reads as being in serious trouble, but it means placed in a grave, i.e. buried.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, i.e. to place a body in its grave.

clue.text: Kind of butterfly naturalist named

definitions.meaning: the large and small ... are common cabbage butterflies
Gilbert ... was the 18th-century English naturalist of Selborne

explanation.surface: A butterfly species named after the naturalist who described it.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabbage butterfly family is named for its pale wings, and Gilbert of Selborne bore that surname.

clue.text: Wicked relative meanly cutting me off

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative

indicators.note: cutting with off means removing part of the following word
together with cutting, signals that letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wicked uncle who meanly disinherits the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' and 'off' are split by the word me, which is the piece removed, leaving ANLY; 'Wicked' is the definition, not a description of the uncle.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncleanly means morally impure, which is close in sense to sinful or wicked.

clue.text: The rest have accommodation around university

indicators.note: the lodging word goes round the letter for university

parts.note: to reside is to live or have lodgings somewhere

explanation.surface: The remaining students have rooms near the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps RESIDE round U: RESID-U-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains, the remainder left over.

clue.text: Emblems of war, 11 and 19 across — or alternatives to them

definitions.meaning: the white and red flowers were the badges of York and Lancaster in the Wars of the ...
rosé wines are a pink alternative to white and red

explanation.surface: Badges of a civil war, coloured white and red, or substitutes for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is WHITE and 19 across is RED; the second reading takes them as wines, to which rosés (accent ignored) are an alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: The York and Lancaster badges were flowers, and pink wines sit between white and red.

clue.text: Concerned with food that's hot in place that's hot

indicators.note: the letter for hot is placed inside the hot-region word

parts.note: the tropics are the hot regions near the equator
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A culinary remark about hot food in a hot country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts H inside TROPIC: TROP-H-IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Trophic is the biological term relating to nutrition and feeding.

clue.text: About to call up — ring — versatile performer

parts.note: on means about, concerning

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to name is to call
a band is a ring, like a wedding band

explanation.surface: Someone about to telephone a gifted entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses only the verb, giving EMAN; 'call up' looks like telephoning, but 'up' does the reversing on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A street musician playing several instruments at once is the very model of a versatile performer.

clue.text: Rivals seeking mates, 11 and 26

definitions.meaning: opponents at the board game each try to checkmate the other
the two sides in the game are called white and black

explanation.surface: Competitors looking for partners, one white and one black.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is WHITE and 26 is BLACK. 'Mates' looks like partners or friends, but it is checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Game opponents aim for checkmate, and the two sides are always named for their colours.

clue.text: Runway for take-off?

definitions.meaning: an airstrip is a runway
to take off clothes

explanation.definitionFit: An airfield runway is called a landing strip, and undressing is stripping.

clue.text: In a way, allowed game of two halves, 19 across and 26

definitions.text: game of two halves, 19 across and 26

indicators.note: the permission word is placed in the path word

parts.note: a route is a way
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A football-style game of two halves, red and black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' sits at the start yet signals the container. 19 across is RED and 26 BLACK: the roulette wheel's pockets alternate between those colours.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino wheel game divides its numbers half red and half black.

clue.text: Off colour?

parts.note: read as the colour that means stop or off, as on a traffic light or switch

explanation.definitionFit: This colour signals stop or off on traffic lights and warning lamps.

clue.text: Was annoyed by being shown topless

indicators.note: topless in a down clue means the first letter goes

parts.note: presented means shown

explanation.surface: Someone offended by a display of nudity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes P from PRESENTED; it looks like nudity but just beheads the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to be annoyed or aggrieved by it.

clue.text: Girl's name I found in fashion magazine

indicators.note: the letter I is located inside the magazine title

parts.note: Elle is a well-known fashion magazine

explanation.surface: Someone spotting a girl's name in a glossy magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts I inside ELLE: ELL-I-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellie is a familiar female given name, short for Eleanor.

clue.text: Settles parts of crossword, 11 and 26

definitions.meaning: to square a bill or debt is to settle it
the grid is made of white and black cells
a chessboard has white and black ones

explanation.surface: Settling the parts of a crossword, white and black.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is WHITE and 26 is BLACK.
explanation.definitionFit: To square an account is to settle it; a crossword grid is made of light and dark cells.

clue.text: See 16
Pelt that may be 11, 19 across, or 26

definitions.meaning: to pelt is to ... with missiles
the spice comes as white, red or black varieties

explanation.surface: An animal skin that might be white, red or black.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is WHITE, 19 across RED, 26 BLACK. 'Pelt' looks like a hide, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper with stones is to pelt, and the seasoning comes in white, red and black forms.

clue.text: Allow shelter and medication, dropping extreme temperatures

indicators.note: each word loses its end letters, both being the abbreviation for temperature

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
a tablet is a pill of medication

explanation.surface: Permitting refuge and medicine, but without the extreme heat or cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping extreme temperatures' removes T from each end of TENT and TABLET, leaving EN and ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable is to make possible, to allow something to happen.

clue.text: With reform of free NHS ahead, do this to feel better

indicators.note: reform means a reorganisation, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
up means ahead, as in a team being two goals up

explanation.surface: A politician claiming that with a free health service reformed, people will feel better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform of' shuffles FREE NHS to FRESHEN; the NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing and tidying oneself to feel refreshed is the phrasal verb's meaning.

clue.text: See 9
Contest that can be 11 or 19 across, intensely so

definitions.meaning: a qualifying round of a race

definitions.text: that can be 11 or 19 across, intensely so
definitions.meaning: white ... and red ... are intense temperatures of glowing metal

explanation.surface: A competition that can become fiercely white- or red-hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is WHITE and 19 across is RED.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary race round is a heat, and white or red heat describe intense temperature.

clue.text: Polish the most valuable pot

definitions.meaning: to ... boots is to polish them with ...
in snooker the darkest ball scores seven points, the highest

explanation.surface: Shine up the most precious cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a cue game; to pot is to sink a ball, and the black is worth most. 'Polish' could be the nationality, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoe blacking is a polish, and the highest-scoring snooker ball is the dark one.

clue.text: One opens with these piano pieces, 11 and 26

definitions.meaning: locks are opened with these
the piano has white and black ones

explanation.surface: A concert opening with white and black piano pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is WHITE and 26 is BLACK. 'pieces' suggests compositions, but they are the parts struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Doors are unlocked with these, and a keyboard has ivory and ebony ones.

clue.text: Bodily cavities revealed in course of organ transplant

indicators.note: the letters are exposed running through the words organ transplant

explanation.surface: Cavities in the body exposed during transplant surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Antra is the plural of antrum, an anatomical cavity such as a sinus.

clue.text: Peter, in rally, starts off, never finishing

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the three words is removed

explanation.surface: Peter competing in a motor rally keeps starting off but never finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts off' removes P, I and R from PETER IN RALLY, leaving ETER N ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes on eternally never comes to an end.
